speaker_role: test-prep/consultancy marketer (Rob Franek, Editor-in-Chief, The Princeton Review)
commercial_incentive: Yes - closes by directing viewers to princetonreview.com and the company's book
key_insights: Lists six ranked factors admissions committees weigh: (1) high school transcript/GPA as the single most important and consistent factor, answering whether the student challenged themselves; (2) SAT/ACT scores (and to a lesser degree AP/Subject Tests), described as still influential even at some test-optional schools for scholarship money; (3) the college essay as a unique personal window; (4) recommendation letters, with the practical tip to follow the exact number requested rather than over-submitting; (5) demonstrated interest, noting that interactions with a college (fairs, interviews, class visits) are increasingly tracked and used to gauge likelihood to enroll; (6) extracurricular activity list, meant to be as individual as the essay
Frames the process as part-quantitative (GPA, test scores) and part fundamentally human/judgment-based, not a pure formula
notable_or_distinctive: A concise, plainly stated ranked framework (six factors in priority order) from a well-known test-prep company executive, useful as a quick orientation checklist rather than deep-dive advice.
reliability_notes: Very short, generic overview with no specific data, school examples, or dates (video is roughly 8 years old per manifest, and admissions practices such as test-optional/demonstrated-interest tracking have evolved significantly since); functions as a promotional teaser for Princeton Review's other content.
